narrative.text: The attack came without warning. An explosion near the palace, or a shooter in the capital, or an attempt on your life during a public appearance — the details blur in the chaos of the aftermath. What matters is this: someone tried to kill the Chancellor of the Republic of Veltria, and they failed. But the attempt itself has changed everything.

You survived. But survival has a price. The doctors say the nerve damage is permanent. Your right hand trembles when you try to hold a pen. The hearing in your left ear is gone, replaced by a flat, ringing tone that the medications cannot quiet. You are alive, but the body you inhabited this morning is no longer the one you govern from.

I look at my hand. It shakes. I tell it to stop, and it does not. This is the cost of the mandate. They tried to kill me, and they succeeded in marking me. Every time I sign a decree, the pen will tremble. Every time someone speaks to my left, I will have to turn my head. I am still the Chancellor. But I am no longer whole.

Chancellor. The situation is contained but the political dimension is not. The Assembly is calling for a response. The press is demanding answers. The military is at elevated readiness. We need to decide — now — whether this government responds with emergency powers, legal process, or public unity. The next hour will define the rest of your Chancellorship.

choices.text: "Convene the emergency cabinet. Every minister, every security chief. We make no statements until we have a plan."
